project_specification.project_name: nullius — gVisor executor for agent-authored signals (orchestrator member, spec C)
project_specification.addition_summary: Run model-authored signal code the way docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md section 5.2 requires: - Isolation: gVisor (runsc). - Network: a namespace with no interfaces. - Filesystem: no mounts; data arrives over IPC only. - Resources: cgroup v2 cpu.max, memory.max and pids.max. - Determinism: thread pins, seeded, and no wall clock. Today nothing launches runsc. The evaluator's SignalSandbox is a plain subprocess with four defects that model-written code can exploit: - It hands the child the whole host environment (API keys, DATABASE_URL). - It never blocks imports inside the child, because exec runs with full builtins. - It reads the result from stdout, which the signal can also write to. - It leaves POLARS_MAX_THREADS unset. The sandbox member holds the policies (isolation, network, imports, budget, timeout, pinning, seed and fail class) as decision-only laws with no caller. This spec adds, in the orchestrator member and without editing the evaluator or sandbox members (Z0): - a hardened child bootstrap; - a hardened subprocess executor, which the "unisolated" mode now uses in place of the evaluator's default; - an OCI bundle generator; - GVisorSandbox, which runs the same bootstrap under runsc; - executor selection from the evaluation context; - a hostile-signal suite, and a runsc integration test that runs only where runsc is installed.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace / Polars + pyarrow / pytest (ruff conventions). runsc release-20260928.0 IS installed on the development host (rootless works via an AppArmor userns profile), and the runtime root is provisioned at /opt/nullius/gvisor-runtime by deploy/gvisor/provision_runtime.sh; docker is not installed.
existing_context.test_baseline: Measured 2026-10-05 on main (HEAD e4cd033): workspace tests/ 1614 passed; packages/orchestrator/tests 133, evaluator 558, nulloracle 1340, ledger 469, signal-agent 761, providers 1382 passed (member suites with -n 4).
existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md: members only; components via create_app().get(name); typed refusals with a code word in the raising module; and no network or credential in tests.
Existing pieces (read, never edit): - evaluator.execute_signal(resolution, code, *, seed, rebalance_dates=None, sandbox=None, materialize=None) calls sandbox.run(code, window, *, seed). It reads result.scores (pl.Series or None), result.problems (list), result.seed and result.contract_version. - The window has to_arrow(), which gives Arrow IPC framed by contract/payload.py (magic NLSWIPC), and universe. - The evaluator's SandboxLimits(wall_s=30, cpu_s=30, mem_mb=4096, pids=32, network=False, filesystem=False), and its fail classes timeout, oom, crash, violation, payload and empty. - The child contract today: - MarketWindowPayload.from_bytes(data).materialize() rebuilds the window; - the SIGNAL_ENTRYPOINT function is called as fn(window, seed); - validate_signal_return(result, window.universe) checks the return. - sandbox member laws, used here as configuration sources: - SandboxImports.screen(source) and imports_allowlist.json; - budget_policy.json (cpu_s 30, mem_mb 2048, pids 32, runner_mem_mb 4096) and timeout_policy.json (wall_s 30); - pinning_policy.json (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, the POLARS_MAX_THREADS floor); - SandboxSeed (NULLIUS_SIGNAL_SEED); - NetworkNamespace(...).specification() -> {"NetworkMode": "none"}; - isolation_policy.json (mechanism gvisor, runtime runsc). - The committed syscalls allowlist would kill CPython+polars (it lacks openat, clone and getrandom). gVisor's Sentry is the syscall boundary, so it is not applied here. Reconciling it is out of scope. - orchestrator (spec A): EvaluationContext.sandbox_runtime ("gvisor" or "unisolated"), and evaluate_node, which calls execute_signal.

category.name: Hardened Child
category.feature: System runs one signal inside a sandbox process through the bootstrap orchestrator/_sandbox_child.py, run as `python -I _sandbox_child.py` (not -S: the runtime's packages live in dist-packages, which site adds). It writes exactly one framed result to a private descriptor, never to stdout. - Input: one length-framed request on stdin: the signal source, the seed, and the NLSWIPC window payload. Nothing travels in the environment except the pins and NULLIUS_SIGNAL_SEED. - Before running any agent code, the bootstrap: - duplicates fd 1 to a private descriptor, and points fd 1 and fd 2 at /dev/null, so the signal's prints cannot reach the result channel; - installs an import guard (a meta-path finder plus a builtins.__import__ wrapper) that admits only the modules imports_allowlist.json lists, and the modules polars, numpy and pyarrow themselves load. The agent's own top-level imports are still checked by name; - removes open, exec, eval, compile, input, breakpoint and __import__ access from the builtins the signal sees; - builds the window from the payload. - It then executes the source in a fresh module namespace, calls signal(window, seed), and validates the return. - Output: one framed JSON result (fail_class, detail, base64 scores, contract_version) on the private descriptor. The fail classes match the evaluator's: timeout, oom, crash, violation, payload and empty. - The bootstrap imports only the standard library, polars, pyarrow and the contract member's payload and signal modules. - Tests run it in a plain subprocess with framed requests. - This feature claims packages/orchestrator/pyproject.toml so that no other feature touches it, and it leaves the file unchanged: the executor adds no dependency.

System creates each signal's result in a hardened subprocess with orchestrator._hardened_sandbox.HardenedSubprocessSandbox(limits=None). It is a drop-in for execute_signal's sandbox argument: run(code, window, *, seed) answers an object with scores, problems, seed, contract_version, fail_class and detail. - The child is spawned with feature 1's bootstrap, and with an environment built from scratch, never copied from os.environ: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, POLARS_MAX_THREADS=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, NULLIUS_SIGNAL_SEED, and nothing else. - Limits come from the sandbox member's policies: RLIMIT_CPU (cpu_s), RLIMIT_AS (runner_mem_mb), RLIMIT_NPROC (pids), RLIMIT_FSIZE (0), and a wall-clock watchdog (wall_s) that kills the process group. - The child starts in a new session, in an empty temporary working directory, with stdin closed after the request. - The result is read only from the private descriptor. stdout and stderr are discarded, capped at 64 KiB each. - A child that exits without writing a result is classified crash (or timeout or oom, by signal and limit). - Before spawning, the code is screened with sandbox.SandboxImports. A disallowed import answers fail_class crash with a detail naming disallowed_import, without spawning.

category.name: gVisor Executor
category.feature: System creates an OCI runtime bundle for one signal run with orchestrator._oci_bundle.build_bundle(directory, *, runtime_root, child_path, limits, lake_roots). It writes config.json and answers its path. - The process is args [/usr/bin/python3, "-I", child_path], with the env of feature 2 exactly, cwd "/tmp", user 65534:65534, noNewPrivileges true, and terminal false. - The root is runtime_root, the read-only runtime root that deploy/gvisor/provision_runtime.sh builds (default /opt/nullius/gvisor-runtime): Ubuntu noble minbase, python3 3.12, polars and pyarrow at uv.lock's pins, and the contract and app packages in /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages. It has no numpy, matching the evaluator's environment. Mounts are only proc, a 64 MiB tmpfs at /tmp, and child_path bound read-only. There is no bind of any host data directory. - Namespaces are pid, ipc, uts, mount and network. The empty network namespace leaves only loopback, so there is no egress, matching the network law. - linux.resources: memory.limit is runner_mem_mb MiB, pids.limit is pids, and the cpu quota is 1 CPU, all from the sandbox member's policies. - The bundle refuses, with BundleError (code word oci_bundle), any configuration whose root or mount source lies under one of lake_roots, or that adds a mount beyond the three listed. - The JSON is deterministic for equal inputs. Tests are pure and need no runsc.

System executes a signal under gVisor with orchestrator._gvisor.GVisorSandbox(*, runsc, runtime_root, state_root, limits=None, lake_roots=()). It is the same drop-in interface as HardenedSubprocessSandbox. - For each run it builds a fresh bundle with feature 4, and launches `runsc --rootless --network=none --root STATE run --bundle BUNDLE ID`. ID is a uuid4. - It writes the framed request to the container's stdin, reads the framed result from the container's stdout pipe (the bootstrap points the signal's fd 1 and fd 2 at /dev/null, so only the bootstrap's private duplicate writes there), applies the wall watchdog with `runsc kill`, and always runs `runsc delete -force` and removes the bundle. - It runs the same SandboxImports screen first. Fail classes are as in feature 2, plus sandbox_escape when runsc reports a sandbox violation. - A missing or non-executable runsc raises GVisorUnavailableError (code word isolation_required) at construction. - Tests inject a fake runsc executable, a script that runs the bootstrap directly, and assert the exact argv, the bundle contents, the cleanup, and that no environment variable from the parent leaks into the spawned command.

System emits a skip reason naming the missing piece, or a passing verdict against a real runsc, in packages/orchestrator/tests/test_gvisor_runsc.py. - The test is skipped, with a reason naming the missing piece, unless runsc is on PATH and NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT names a provisioned runtime. - When it runs, a benign signal scores, and is deterministic across two runs. - A socket connection and a read of a planted lake directory both fail, and the import guard refuses `import os`. - An infinite loop is a timeout, and the container state directory is empty afterwards.

category.name: Executor Selection
category.feature: System creates the signal executor from the evaluation context: orchestrator._context.signal_sandbox(context) answers a GVisorSandbox for sandbox_runtime "gvisor", or a HardenedSubprocessSandbox for "unisolated". - "gvisor" also needs gvisor_runtime_root, gvisor_state_root and lake_roots from the evaluation config, and refuses with EvaluationConfigError naming the missing key. - evaluate_node always passes signal_sandbox(context) to execute_signal. The evaluator's default SignalSandbox is never used for agent code. - The fail_class and detail that the executor reports are carried into NodeEvaluation.fail_class. The evaluator's RawScoreVector drops them, so evaluate_node reads them from the executor's last result. - Every existing orchestrator test stays green.

project_specification.integration_points: New modules in packages/orchestrator: _sandbox_child, _hardened_sandbox, _oci_bundle and _gvisor. Feature 7 edits _context.py and _evaluate.py, both from spec A. The new tests are test_hostile_signals and test_gvisor_runsc (skipped without runsc). Provisioning runsc and the read-only runtime root (NULLIUS_GVISOR_RUNTIME_ROOT) on a host is an operator step, and so is building a digest-pinned runner image. Every new file is committed as an empty stub so its claim resolves.
project_specification.constraints: - Agent-authored code never runs in the orchestrator process, and never in a child whose environment was copied from the parent. - Do not edit the evaluator, sandbox, contract or nulloracle members, or the root pyproject.toml. - No host data directory is mounted into a gVisor bundle. The data lake reaches a signal only as the IPC window. - No test opens a network connection to a non-loopback host, or reads a real credential. No third-party dependency is added. - Do not edit run.sh, the .env templates, claw-forge.yaml or docs/user-journeys/. - All existing workspace tests and the orchestrator and evaluator member suites stay green.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 2: the hardened subprocess executor (feature 2) and the OCI bundle (feature 4).
Phase 3: the hostile-signal suite (feature 3) and the gVisor executor (feature 5).
Phase 4: the runsc integration test (feature 6) and executor selection (feature 7).
